close_reason: P4 readability finding in convergence territory. The bead correctly identifies a test-form choice: byte-equal-against-input (current) vs structural-equality-plus-separate-wrapper-key-assertion (proposed). Both prove that #[serde(transparent)] is in effect. The current form has inline comments documenting the BTreeMap-alphabetical-key constraint (task.rs lines 237-242 explain it explicitly). The proposed refactor would not strictly improve correctness; it would relocate the assertion shape. Per /do-beads convergence rule, P4 stylistic refactors that don't change tested behavior or correctness are bikeshed territory. Closing without code action; the next contributor adding a similar test should use the inline comment block as the convention guide.
description:
In tests/types_test.rs, both `task_recurrence_overrides_patch_object_transparent` (line 244) and `task_localizations_patch_object_transparent` (line 280) construct fixtures with alphabetically-sorted inner keys and assert byte-equal round-trip after serialize.

The tests carry inline comments explaining why ("without the preserve_order feature on serde_json — is a BTreeMap and emits keys in alphabetical order"), but a future contributor copying this pattern for a new test type may not notice the constraint until their byte-equal assertion fails on a non-alphabetical fixture.

What would make it clear: a tiny helper in the test module that documents and applies the constraint, e.g. `fn assert_byte_equal_roundtrip_alphabetical_keys(json: &str)` — and a more prominent module-level doc comment near the top of the test file. Alternatively, the tests could assert `serde_json::from_str(&serialized) == serde_json::from_str(json)` (structural equality) instead of byte-equal, which is the actual semantic intent and is robust to map ordering.

The byte-equal form does prove that `#[serde(transparent)]` is in effect (which is its stated purpose), but a structural-equality + separate "must not have wrapper keys" assertion would prove the same thing without the ordering trap.
title: PatchObject transparent round-trip test relies on alphabetical key ordering
